title: B-Cell Translocations and the CD10 Trap: Mantle Cell, Follicular, Burkitt and B-ALL
summary: Separate CD10-positive follicular lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma and B-lymphoblastic leukemia with TdT, BCL2 and proliferation, and match mantle cell, follicular and Burkitt lymphoma and B-ALL to their defining translocations and risk.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 34 Hit 9 (mantle cell t(11;14), follicular t(14;18), Burkitt t(8;14)), Hit 17 (t(12;21) ETV6-RUNX1 in B-ALL vs Philadelphia-positive ALL) and Exam Trap 6 (CD10+ B-cell neoplasm), checked against WHO-HAEM5 lymphoid (Alaggio 2022), Gajzer & Fromm 2025, Chiaretti 2014, Terwilliger 2017, Sun 2017, Kalisz 2019 and Ladha 2019. The reviewer presents marker and translocation associations as invariant; sources give ≥ 95% (MCL t(11;14)), ~85% (FL t(14;18)) and ~90% (FL CD10), and non-nodal MCL is often CD5-negative. Hit 17 calls ETV6-RUNX1 favourable without noting late relapses (up to 20%, Sun 2017). Not taught: bcl-6 in follicular lymphoma (Hit 9) — not checked. CLL vs mantle cell flow is taught in heme-bcell-neoplasm-phenotypes.

objectives: Use TdT, CD34, surface light chain, BCL2 and Ki-67 to separate CD10-positive follicular lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma and B-lymphoblastic leukemia.
Match mantle cell, follicular and Burkitt lymphoma to t(11;14) IGH::CCND1, t(14;18) IGH::BCL2 and IG::MYC.
Contrast ETV6::RUNX1 and BCR::ABL1 B-lymphoblastic leukemia by age group and risk.

scenes.title: Three CD10-positive clones
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three flow cytometry reports, all showing CD10-positive B cells. (1) A 58-year-old with painless enlarged lymph nodes: CD10+, CD5−, kappa-restricted, BCL2 increased compared with background T cells. (2) A 9-year-old with a fast-growing abdominal mass: CD10+, CD5−, lambda-restricted, TdT−, no BCL2 over-expression, Ki-67 above 95%. (3) A 4-year-old with marrow blasts: CD19+, CD10+, TdT+, CD34+, no surface light chain. Question token: “Same CD10, same disease?”

cues.text: Three reports, all with CD10-positive B cells. A fifty-eight-year-old with painless nodes: kappa-restricted, with increased BCL2.
A nine-year-old with a fast-growing abdominal mass: lambda-restricted, TdT negative, and a Ki-67 above ninety-five percent.
And a four-year-old with marrow blasts that carry TdT and CD34. Same CD10. Is it the same disease?

scenes.title: Mature or precursor?
scenes.altText: Schematic cards. Flow cytometry sorts mature B-cell lymphomas into CD5+/CD10−, CD10+/CD5−, CD5−/CD10− and large-cell/plasmacytic groups (Gajzer & Fromm 2025). Mature lymphoma card: monotypic surface light chain (kappa or lambda), and with rare exceptions no TdT or CD34. Precursor card: most ALL express TdT; earliest B-lineage markers CD19, CD22 and CD79a; CD10 defines the “common” ALL subgroup (EGIL B-II); pro-B ALL is CD10−. Summary token: TdT/CD34 point to lymphoblasts; light-chain restriction points to a mature lymphoma.

cues.text: Flow cytometry sorts mature B-cell lymphomas by two markers, CD5 and CD10. Follicular lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma fall in the CD10-positive, CD5-negative group.
Mature lymphoma cells carry surface light chain restricted to kappa or to lambda, and, with rare exceptions, they lack the immaturity markers TdT and CD34.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia is a precursor neoplasm. Most cases express TdT, with the B-lineage markers CD19, CD22 and CD79a. CD10 marks the common subgroup; the earliest pro-B type lacks it.
So CD10 does not name one disease. TdT and CD34 point toward lymphoblasts; light-chain restriction without TdT points toward a mature lymphoma.

scenes.title: Translocation fingerprints
scenes.altText: Three fingerprint cards. Mantle cell: t(11;14)(q13;q32) IGH::CCND1 in ≥95% of cases, cyclin D1 over-expression; CD5+, CD23−, CD200−, normal-to-bright CD20, FMC7+; confirm with cyclin D1 or SOX11 immunohistochemistry or FISH; non-nodal MCL frequently lacks CD5 and SOX11 (WHO-HAEM5). Follicular: t(14;18)(q32;q21) IGH::BCL2 in about 85% (classic FL); CD10 in about 90%; CD5−; BCL2 increased versus background T cells. Burkitt: IG::MYC juxtaposition, most commonly t(8;14); CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2 negative or weak, Ki-67 above 95%; “starry sky” from histiocytes engulfing apoptotic tumour cells; doubling time 24–48 hours. Split card: follicular vs Burkitt = BCL2 (increased vs absent/weak) and a Ki-67 above 95% in Burkitt.

cues.text: Now the fingerprints. Mantle cell lymphoma carries t(11;14), fusing IGH with CCND1 in at least ninety-five percent of cases, so cyclin D1 is over-expressed. It is CD5 positive but CD23 and CD200 negative, though the non-nodal form often lacks CD5.

Classic follicular lymphoma carries t(14;18), IGH with BCL2, in about eighty-five percent of cases. About ninety percent express CD10, CD5 is negative, and BCL2 is increased compared with background T cells.

Burkitt lymphoma juxtaposes MYC with an immunoglobulin gene, most often by t(8;14). It is CD10 and BCL6 positive, BCL2 negative or weak, with a Ki-67 above ninety-five percent. Histiocytes swallowing dying tumour cells give the starry sky.

So follicular and Burkitt share CD10 but split on BCL2 and proliferation: increased BCL2 in follicular lymphoma; little or no BCL2 and near-total Ki-67 in Burkitt, whose cells double in one to two days.

scenes.title: B-ALL genetics and the hook answers
scenes.altText: Genetics cards. ETV6::RUNX1, t(12;21): about 25% of childhood ALL diagnosed at ages 2–10 years (median 4); the most common fusion gene of childhood ALL; generally favourable long-term remission and survival, but late relapses in up to 20%; relatively rare in adults. BCR::ABL1, t(9;22): 15–50% of adult ALL, rising with age; historical 1-year survival around 10%, improved with tyrosine kinase inhibitors; Ph status must be known before treatment; often CD34+, CD10+ with CD13/CD33. Testing token: karyotype fails if blasts do not enter metaphase; FISH detects nearly all investigated ALL abnormalities (about 99% sensitivity). Hook answers: (1) follicular pattern, confirm t(14;18) and tissue; (2) Burkitt pattern, confirm MYC by FISH and tissue; (3) B-lymphoblastic leukemia, test for ETV6::RUNX1, BCR::ABL1 and other defining lesions.

cues.text: In B-lymphoblastic leukemia, genetics set the risk. ETV6::RUNX1, from t(12;21), is the most common fusion in childhood ALL: about a quarter of cases between ages two and ten. It generally carries favourable remission and survival, but late relapses occur in up to twenty percent.

BCR::ABL1, the Philadelphia translocation t(9;22), is the opposite: fifteen to fifty percent of adult ALL, rising with age, with historically poor survival that tyrosine kinase inhibitors have improved. Ph status must be known before treatment starts.
Conventional karyotype fails if blasts do not divide. FISH detects nearly all the investigated ALL abnormalities.

Back to the hook. The adult has a follicular lymphoma pattern; the nine-year-old, a Burkitt pattern; both need MYC or BCL2 testing and tissue to confirm. The four-year-old has B-lymphoblastic leukemia: test the blasts for ETV6::RUNX1 and BCR::ABL1.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “CD10+ B cells = follicular lymphoma” (✓ Burkitt lymphoma and B-lymphoblastic leukemia are CD10+ too; use TdT, BCL2, Ki-67 and the translocation); “TdT-negative blasts = B-ALL anyway” (✓ TdT negativity is the rule in Burkitt leukemia; investigate TdT-negative cases for a mature aggressive lymphoma); “Every B-ALL translocation is bad news” (✓ ETV6::RUNX1 is generally favourable; BCR::ABL1 is the high-risk one).

cues.text: Trap one: CD10-positive B cells mean follicular lymphoma. No: Burkitt lymphoma and B-lymphoblastic leukemia are CD10 positive too. Check TdT, BCL2, Ki-67 and the translocation.
Trap two: TdT-negative blasts are still B-ALL. No: TdT negativity is the rule in Burkitt leukemia, so a TdT-negative case needs work-up for a mature aggressive lymphoma.
Trap three: every translocation in B-ALL is bad news. No: ETV6::RUNX1 is generally favourable; BCR::ABL1 is the high-risk one.

scenes.title: The chromosome 14 loudspeaker
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Chromosome 14 holds the IGH loudspeaker. Whatever gene is moved next to it gets shouted: cyclin D1 from 11 in mantle cell, BCL2 from 18 in follicular, MYC from 8 in Burkitt. The 12;21 swap in children is the good-news ticket.” Tokens: 11;14 = cyclin D1 · 14;18 = BCL2 · 8;14 = MYC · 12;21 = good news. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: chromosome fourteen holds the IGH loudspeaker. Whatever gene is moved next to it gets shouted: cyclin D1 from eleven in mantle cell, BCL2 from eighteen in follicular, MYC from eight in Burkitt. The twelve twenty-one swap in children is the good-news ticket.

Where it breaks: MYC can pair with other immunoglobulin genes; some mantle cell and about fifteen percent of follicular lymphomas lack the classic translocation; and t(12;21) does not involve IGH at all, and can still relapse late.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “CD10+ = follicular, Burkitt or B-ALL → check TdT, BCL2, Ki-67”, “t(11;14) mantle · t(14;18) follicular · MYC Burkitt · t(12;21) favourable B-ALL”.

cues.text: CD10 marks follicular lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma and B-lymphoblastic leukemia alike, so separate them with TdT, BCL2, proliferation and the translocation: t(14;18) for follicular, MYC for Burkitt, and t(12;21) for the generally favourable childhood leukemia.

props.label: CD10+ = follicular, Burkitt or B-ALL → TdT, BCL2, Ki-67

explanation.what: Plain language: CD10 is a surface marker shared by some mature lymphomas and by immature leukemia cells, so it cannot name the disease by itself. Immaturity markers, survival and growth proteins, and the chromosome swap that drives each cancer finish the job. Scientific terms: CD10 (CALLA), terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT), CD34, surface light-chain restriction, BCL2, BCL6, Ki-67, IGH::CCND1 t(11;14), IGH::BCL2 t(14;18), IG::MYC t(8;14), ETV6::RUNX1 t(12;21), BCR::ABL1 t(9;22), FISH.
explanation.why: Translocations that place CCND1, BCL2 or MYC next to an immunoglobulin gene drive over-expression of cyclin D1 (cell cycle), BCL2 (survival) or MYC (proliferation), which explains each lymphoma’s phenotype. In B-lymphoblastic leukemia, the fusion defines the subtype and much of the risk.
explanation.measure: Flow cytometry: CD5/CD10 grouping, light-chain restriction, TdT/CD34, BCL2 intensity. Immunohistochemistry: cyclin D1, SOX11, Ki-67. Genetics: FISH for t(11;14), t(14;18), MYC rearrangement; ETV6::RUNX1 and BCR::ABL1 in B-ALL (FISH detects nearly all investigated ALL abnormalities; karyotype fails without metaphases).
explanation.differs: Follicular (CD10+ in ~90%, BCL2 increased, t(14;18) ~85%) vs Burkitt (CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2 negative/weak, Ki-67 > 95%, IG::MYC) vs B-ALL (CD10± , TdT+, CD34+, no surface light chain); mantle cell (CD5+, CD23−, cyclin D1+, t(11;14) ≥ 95%); ETV6::RUNX1 (childhood, generally favourable) vs BCR::ABL1 (adult, rising with age, historically poor).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: name the lymphoma from a CD10+ phenotype with BCL2/Ki-67 clues, match a translocation to its disease, or state the prognosis of t(12;21) vs t(9;22) in B-ALL.

mnemonic.text: Chromosome 14 holds the IGH loudspeaker. Whatever gene is moved next to it gets shouted: cyclin D1 from 11 in mantle cell, BCL2 from 18 in follicular, MYC from 8 in Burkitt. The 12;21 swap in children is the good-news ticket.
mnemonic.explanation: Links each translocation partner to the over-expressed protein and the lymphoma, and marks t(12;21) as the favourable B-ALL lesion.
mnemonic.limitation: MYC can pair with other immunoglobulin genes; some mantle cell lymphomas and about 15% of follicular lymphomas lack the classic translocation; t(12;21) does not involve IGH and late relapses occur.

analogyLimitations: Cards are schematic; no micrographs or real flow plots.
The loudspeaker is a simplification of enhancer-driven over-expression.
takeaway: CD10 marks follicular lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma and B-lymphoblastic leukemia alike, so separate them with TdT, BCL2, proliferation and the translocation: t(14;18) for follicular, MYC for Burkitt, and t(12;21) for the generally favourable childhood leukemia.

questions.stem: A lymph-node mass in a child shows medium-sized B cells that are CD10+, CD5−, lambda-restricted and TdT−, with BCL2 negative, Ki-67 above 95% and a “starry sky” pattern. Which diagnosis fits best?

options.rationale: Correct. CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2 negative/weak, Ki-67 > 95% and starry sky fit Burkitt; confirm IG::MYC by FISH.
Incorrect. Follicular lymphoma is CD10+ too, but shows increased BCL2 and usually t(14;18), without the Burkitt Ki-67 above 95%.
Incorrect. B-ALL blasts usually express TdT and lack surface light-chain restriction.
Incorrect. Mantle cell lymphoma is typically CD5+ and CD10−, with cyclin D1 over-expression.

questions.stem: Marrow blasts from a 4-year-old are CD19+, CD10+, TdT+ and carry ETV6::RUNX1 from t(12;21). What does the genetic finding indicate?

options.text: A generally favourable childhood B-ALL subtype, though late relapse can occur
options.rationale: Correct. ETV6::RUNX1 is the most common childhood ALL fusion and generally favourable, with late relapses in up to 20%.

options.text: Philadelphia-positive ALL needing a tyrosine kinase inhibitor
options.rationale: Incorrect. Philadelphia-positive ALL is BCR::ABL1 from t(9;22), not t(12;21).

options.text: A mature B-cell lymphoma in leukemic phase
options.rationale: Incorrect. TdT positivity marks precursor lymphoblasts, not a mature lymphoma.

options.text: The highest-risk B-ALL subtype of adults
options.rationale: Incorrect. t(12;21) is relatively rare in adults; BCR::ABL1 is the classic high-risk adult lesion.

questions.stem: A CD5+, CD23−, CD200− B-cell lymphoma strongly expresses cyclin D1. Which translocation is expected?

options.rationale: Correct. t(11;14) IGH::CCND1 is present in ≥ 95% of mantle cell lymphoma and drives cyclin D1 over-expression.
Incorrect. This is the hallmark of follicular lymphoma, which is CD10+ and CD5−.
Incorrect. This is the usual Burkitt lymphoma translocation; Burkitt is CD10+ and CD5−.
Incorrect. This is a childhood B-lymphoblastic leukemia fusion, not a mature lymphoma lesion.

claims.text: CD5/CD10 grouping of mature B-cell lymphomas; light-chain restriction; TdT/CD34 absent in mature lymphomas and favouring B-LL.
Most ALL TdT+; CD19, CD22, CD79a; CD10 defines common ALL, pro-B CD10−; TdT negativity is the rule in Burkitt leukemia.
MCL: t(11;14) IGH::CCND1 in ≥ 95%, cyclin D1 over-expression; CD5+, CD23−, CD200−, FMC7+; cyclin D1/SOX11 confirmation; non-nodal MCL often CD5−.
FL: t(14;18) IGH::BCL2 in ~85%; CD10 in ~90%; CD5−; increased BCL2.
Burkitt: IG::MYC, most often t(8;14); CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2−/weak, Ki-67 > 95%; starry sky; doubling time 24–48 h.
ETV6::RUNX1: most common childhood ALL fusion, ~25% at ages 2–10; generally favourable; late relapse up to 20%; rare in adults.
BCR::ABL1 ALL: 15–50% of adult ALL rising with age; historically poor, improved with TKIs; Ph status before treatment.
Karyotype fails without metaphases; FISH detects nearly all investigated ALL abnormalities (~99%).
Reviewer Hit 9: follicular lymphoma is bcl-6 positive — not checked against an open source; not taught.

accuracyFlags.issue: Hit 17 calls t(12;21) ETV6-RUNX1 a favourable prognosis without qualification. Sun 2017 describes generally favourable remission and survival but late relapses in up to 20% of patients and says the prognostic implication is still debated. The lesson teaches “generally favourable, late relapse possible” (register flag rv-etv6-runx1-late-relapse).

Hit 9 presents mantle cell (CD5+, t(11;14)) and follicular (CD10+, t(14;18)) features as invariant. WHO-HAEM5 gives IGH::CCND1 in ≥ 95% of MCL, notes non-nodal MCL frequently lacks CD5, and gives t(14;18) in ~85% of FL; Gajzer 2025 gives CD10 in ~90% of FL. The lesson teaches the frequencies (register flag rv-bcell-translocation-frequencies).
